sources.headline: Pope Leo resumes work in hospital while recovering from surgery
sources.text: Roman Catholic leader met top Vatican aide, as doctors say recovery proceeding after lung surgery to remove cancerous growth.Pope Leo XIV has resumed work from hospital as the leader of the Roman Catholic Church recovers from surgery to remove a cancerous nodule.Leo met Vatican chief of staff Archbishop Paolo Rudelli at Gemelli hospital in Rome, where he is being treated, the Vatican said on Thursday. The top aide handles much of the day-to-day administrative work of the Holy See.Recommended Stories list of 3 itemslist 1 of 3Pope Leo XIV to undergo surgery after lump found in lunglist 2 of 3Pope Leo continues working after lung surgery announcementlist 3 of 3Pope Leo to undergo surgery to remove lung nodule in Romeend of listAn update from Leo’s personal physician, Dr Luigi Carbone and Dr Stefano Margaritora, the head of thoracic surgery at Gemelli hospital, said the pope’s post-operative tests remained within normal levels and his physiotherapy session on Thursday involved full mobility exercises.Leo was going about his daily activities independently, doctors said.“The chest X-ray revealed good recovery of the operated lung,” they reported. “Overall, his post-operative recovery is proceeding as expected.”For a second day, the pope celebrated Mass with other priests in a special chapel set up near his room on the 10th floor of the hospital, spokesman Matteo Bruni said.The 71-year-old had part of his right lung removed after a lengthy operation on Tuesday following doctors identifying a suspected cancerous nodule.The surgery confirmed he had adenocarcinoma, the most common type of lung cancer.Doctors are still awaiting the results of tests to understand the precise molecular makeup of the cancer, whether it has spread beyond the lobe and whether any further treatment is necessary.Waving to the crowd on the Champs-Elysees in Paris last month [File: Kiran Ridley/AFP]Pope Leo attracted a following of almost one million people at a Mass in Paris during a four-day visit to France last month before announcing he was to undergo surgery.It is unclear whether he will make his planned trip to South American countries next month.Asked if any changes to Leo’s planned trip from November 6-17 were expected, spokesman Bruni pointed to Leo’s words on Sunday when he announced the discovery of the nodule and impending surgery.“Thank you for your prayers for the pastoral visit I will make to Peru,” Leo said on Sunday in Spanish, in a greeting delivered to a Peruvian group. The trip is also scheduled to include Uruguay and Argentina.Leo is expected to remain in hospital until at least next Tuesday.

sources.headline: While Pope Leo Recovers From Lung Surgery, the Vatican Runs on Autopilot
Pope Leo resumes some papal duties after surgery, Vatican says
sources.text:
By
Kerry Breen
News Editor
Kerry Breen is a news editor at CBSNews.com. A graduate of New York University's Arthur L. Carter School of Journalism, she previously worked at NBC News' TODAY Digital. She covers current events, breaking news and issues including substance use.
Read Full Bio
October 15, 2026 / 12:00 PM EDT
/ CBS News
Add CBS News on Google
Pope Leo XIV has resumed some papal duties, the Vatican said Thursday, after he had a piece of his right lung removed and received a diagnosis of lung cancer earlier this week. A spokesperson for the Vatican said the pope celebrated Mass around noon and began "a little bit of work activity," including reading documents. The pontiff also met with Archbishop Paolo Rudelli, undersecretary of state, on Thursday, the Vatican said. Leo is set to be released from Rome's Gemelli Hospital on Oct. 20, one week after he was first admitted. The Vatican spokesperson said Leo would like to lead the Angelus prayer from the hospital on Sunday, but it's not clear yet whether that will happen. Leo also underwent routine checkups, including a chest X-ray, on Thursday, according to personal physician Dr. Luigi Carbone and thoracic surgeon Dr. Stefano Margaritora. Margaritora led the operation on the pontiff. The X-ray showed "good recovery of the operated lung," the two said in a statement, and the pope's "post-operative recovery is progressing as expected." The pope has also had at least one physiotherapy session, Carbone and Margaritora said. Candida Moss, the Edward Cadbury professor of theology at the University of Birmingham in England, told CBS News on Wednesday that it's typical for popes to stick to their schedules even amid health issues. Vatican protocols call for the pope's cardinals and aide to take over as many duties as possible, Moss said.
An attendee holds a sign for Pope Leo XIV at a football match between Inter Miami CF and New York City FC in Miami, Florida, on Oct. 14, 2026.
CHANDAN KHANNA /AFP via Getty Images
"We have a long tradition of popes — not just Pope Francis, but also Pope John Paul II, who had Parkinson's for 10 years — who continued to remain as active as they could, and as active in Catholic liturgies as they could, right up until the end of their tenures," Moss said.
The Vatican announced Leo had been diagnosed with lung cancer on Tuesday following his surgery.Preoperative tests had indicated the potential presence of the cancer, the Vatican said earlier this week. During the 90-minute operation, a lobe of the pontiff's right lung that had a nodular lesion was removed, the Vatican said. The Vatican has not shared any other details about Leo's cancer, such as its stage or genetic makeup.Leo is expected to travel to South America next month. The Vatican pointed to comments the pontiff made Sunday, when he said he is looking forward to going.
The pope's audiences are canceled through Oct. 20.

sources.headline: Pope Leo to have surgery after lump found on lung
sources.text: Pope Leo XIV has announced he will be operated on "in the coming days" after a nodule was found on his lung during a medical check-up."The doctors found an early, well-localised nodule on my lung," he told the public during his weekly Sunday prayers in St Peter's Square in Rome.The 71-year-old said his medical team "believe it would be right to intervene" and he had agreed to the operation, while reassuring pilgrims that the mass was "well-contained" and caught "at an early stage".The pontiff's admission that he would need surgery comes nearly a year-and-a-half after he succeeded the late Pope Francis, who also experienced issues with his lungs that required hospital treatment.Leo concluded his Angelus prayer by thanking everyone for their "spiritual closeness" and said he entrusted himself to their prayers.Holy See Press Office spokesman Matteo Bruni told the media that "the operation is scheduled for the first days of next week".He added that the Pope is expected to take about a week to recover.Vatican News, the Holy See's news portal, said the operation will take place at Gemelli Hospital in Rome.The hospital set up a special Papal suite following the failed assassination attempt on Pope John Paul II's life in May 1981, which is still in use today.Italy's Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni expressed her "personal solidarity" with the Pope as he "faces the ordeal ahead in the coming days".Her sentiments were echoed by Italian President Sergio Mattarella, who offered his "sincerest wishes for a peaceful recovery and a speedy and full return to health".Isaac Herzog, the president of Israel, also wished the pontiff "a full and speedy recovery".The Pope, born Robert Francis Prevost, is the 267th occupant of the throne of St Peter – the first US citizen to do so.He was ordained in 1982 and spent years as a missionary in Peru, where he is remembered as a figure who worked with marginalised communities.During Sunday's service, the Pope confirmed his upcoming visit to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru in November will still go ahead.The Archbishop of Montevideo, Daniel Sturla, said preparations for his tour will continue with "greater enthusiasm" as he called for prayers for his recovery.A lung nodule is a small lump of tissue that is usually detected following an X-ray or CT scan of the chest, according to the NHS.Most nodules do not cause other symptoms.

sources.headline: Pope Leo XIV to undergo lung surgery this week
sources.text:
Pope Leo XIV to undergo lung surgery this week
Transcript
Download
Embed

Transcript
Pope Leo XIV delivers the Angelus prayer in St. Peter's Square at the Vatican, Sunday, Oct. 11, 2026.
Gregorio Borgia/AP
hide caption
Gregorio Borgia/AP
Pope Leo XIV announced Sunday that he would have surgery this week to remove a "localized nodule" in his lung. Leo said the nodule was found at a "very early stage" with doctors recommending surgery.
"Following their advice, I have therefore decided to undergo an operation to remove it," Leo said during his weekly Sunday noon blessing in St. Peter's Square. The surgery will take place at Rome's Gemelli Hospital, which is the primary location for popes to receive medical attention. "I thank you for your spiritual closeness and entrust myself to your prayers," Leo said to the crowds on Sunday. He later posted the message about his surgery on social media. According to the American Cancer Society, a lung nodule is a small abnormal area, less than or equal to 3 cm, found during a CT scan of the chest or abdomen. These tests are often conducted as routine screenings for "trauma, heart disease, non-cancer related lung disease, or lung infection."
Dr. Panagis Galiatsatos, a pulmonary physician at Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine, said lung nodules are common in older adults. "The majority of lung nodules are benign," Galiatsatos said. "I usually call them the lungs' wrinkles" When they're discovered, doctors will test them to determine whether there is cause for concern. "If they're now discussing that they need to remove the lung nodule, one of his tests must have crossed their threshold … and the suspicion and concern for cancer became a little bit higher," Galiatsatos said. "So that's why he's undergoing this surgery." Vatican spokesperson Matteo Bruni said in a statement that "the operation is scheduled for the first days of this week and the estimated post-operative recovery time will be about one week." Leo's next major international trip is scheduled for early November to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru. It's unclear if the surgery would affect his itinerary. During his papacy, Leo has been outspoken about peace throughout the world. He spent part of his Sunday address renewing calls for peace in Ukraine. "I make a heartfelt appeal to the parties to the conflict to allow the safe transport of grain across the Black Sea," Leo said. "The daily bread of millions of people cannot be held hostage by war."
On Saturday, the Pope also called for the death penalty to be abolished, saying on X that it is "inadmissible because it is an attack on the inviolability and dignity of the person." "The common good can be safeguarded and the requirements of justice can be met without recourse to capital punishment: effective systems of detention have been developed that protect citizens while at the same time do not completely deprive those who are guilty of the possibility of redemption," Leo said.

sources.headline: Pope Leo XIV to have surgery in 'coming days' to remove nodule in lung
sources.text:
Published on 11/10/2026 - 13:02 GMT+2•Updated
13:19
Pope Leo XIV announced on Sunday that he was scheduled to have surgery in the "coming days" to remove a nodule in his lung.
Speaking during his weekly address in St. Peter's Square, the 71-year-old pontiff said the nodule had been discovered during "recent checkups" and that doctors believed it would be best to intervene.
"It was detected at a very early stage and is well localised," he said.
"I have decided to undergo surgery to have it removed," he continued, adding that the procedure was "already scheduled for the coming days."
The operation will reportedly take place at Rome's Gemelli University Hospital.
The Vatican press office told reporters that the procedure is set to take place early in the week and that the expected recovery time is roughly one week.
Chicago-born Leo became pope in 2025 following the death of his predecessor, Francis.
According to the American Lung Association, a lung nodule is a "small mass of dense tissue on the lung" that can be spotted on chest X-rays or CT scans.
It says that while most lung nodules are benign, some can be cancerous.
"If the nodule looks cancerous (malignant) or your health history suggests a higher risk for cancer, physicians will order tests to learn more about your nodule(s)," the association says on its website. "These tests often include a combination of imaging scans, nodule and lymph node biopsies, and sometimes blood tests."
This is a developing story. Please check back here for further details.

Reuters
Published: 6:58pm, 11 Oct 2026Updated: 7:13pm, 11 Oct 2026

Pope Leo said ⁠on Sunday that doctors had detected a small growth on his lung during a recent health check and he would be undergoing surgery this ‌week to remove it, in the first health scare of the 71-year-old pontiff’s tenure.

Leo told pilgrims in St. Peter’s Square for his weekly Sunday prayer that the growth was “well-contained” and caught at an early stage.

“Recently, during ⁠some medical examinations, doctors found a localised nodule in my ‌lung,” said the pontiff. “It was detected at a very early stage and is well ‌contained.”

“The doctors believe it is advisable to intervene, ⁠so, following their ⁠advice, I have decided to undergo surgery to remove it,” he said. “The ‌operation is already scheduled for the next few days.”

A nodule on the lung is ⁠a small, localised ⁠lesion that can be benign. The American Thoracic Society says fewer than 5 per cent of lung nodules overall prove cancerous, ‌although risk rises with age, size, and other factors.

Members of the Peruvian community carry an image of the Lord of Miracles prior to Pope Leo’s prayer in St. Peter Square at the Vatican, on Sunday. Photo: AFP

Leo, elected pope by ‌the world’s ‌cardinals in May 2025, is relatively young for a ‌Church leader. He enjoys sports, including tennis, and is ⁠not known to previously have had health issues.

The late pope ⁠Francis, Leo’s predecessor, died at age 88 and was increasingly frail in his later years.

The Vatican press ‌office said ‌Leo’s recovery from surgery was expected to take about a week. It did not immediately provide further details about the pope’s health.

Leo keeps a busy schedule and is ‌due to make an ‌11-day tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru from November 6 to 17.

Before mentioning his health issue in his address on Sunday, the pope referred to the trip, thanking Catholics for their prayers “for the pastoral visit I will undertake”.

sources.text: VATICAN CITY– Pope Leo said on Oct 11 that doctors had detected a small growth on his lung during a recent health check and he would be undergoing surgery this week to remove it, in the first health scare of the 71-year-old pontiff’s tenure.Leo told pilgrims in St Peter’s Square for his weekly Sunday prayer that the growth was “well-contained” and had been spotted early.The Vatican did not say whether the nodule is believed to be malignant.“Recently, during some medical examinations, doctors found a localised nodule in my lung,” said the pontiff. “It was detected at a very early stage and is well contained.”“The doctors believe it is advisable to intervene, so, following their advice, I have decided to undergo surgery to remove it,” he said. “The operation is already scheduled for the next few days.”A nodule on the lung is a small, localised lesion that can be benign. The American Thoracic Society says fewer than 5% of lung nodules overall prove cancerous, although risk rises with age, size, and other factors such as smoking.Leo, elected pope by the world’s cardinals in May 2025, is relatively young for a Church leader. He enjoys sports, including tennis, and is not known to be a smoker or to previously have had health issues.Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni wished the Pope well.“I would like to express to the Holy Father my personal support, and that of the Italian government, as he faces this challenge in the coming days,” she said in a statement.“The serenity and composure with which he spoke about it during today’s Angelus are reassuring,” Meloni added.The late Pope Francis, Leo’s predecessor, died at age 88 and was increasingly frail in his later years.The Vatican press office said Leo’s recovery from surgery was expected to take about a week. It did not immediately provide further details about the pope’s health.Leo keeps a busy schedule and is due to make an 11-day tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru from Nov 6 to 17.Before mentioning his health issue in his address on Oct 11, the pope referred to the trip, thanking Catholics for their prayers “for the pastoral visit I will undertake.” REUTERS
